scope: Guarded hosted lane A ordinary-member account-popover cases T20, T23 and T26 on a frozen unpublished development v0.2.503 artifact. The native driver completed but the resource final was invalid, so this run earns zero product acceptance credit.
native_observation: The sanitized native receipt has status pass for T20, T23 and T26 and child exit 0. It records an ordinary-member session (access token and profile present, isAdmin=false), one open account menu with Profile, Preferences and Sign out controls, and an active Profile pane with Back and Save profile controls after Profile was clicked. Preferences selected one Settings pane while the member identity remained. Sign out removed the access token and profile, and guest state plus the guest menu persisted after reload. The receipt's build.sourceSha is null; the hosted DEVELOPMENT_TEST_IMPORTED and PREPARED_DEVELOPMENT log lines bind the imported exact-pushed-commit artifact to the tested source above.
failure_boundary: The acceptance resource journal admitted the job, then measured CPU busy/high load repeatedly during Chrome execution. The child finished with exit 0, but the completion recovery window expired with RESOURCE_CPU_CONFIRMATION_EXPIRED, so the journal finalized invalid and the workflow failed. Package and browser resource finals were valid. This is a resource-invalid attempt, not a product or driver failure verdict.

resource_diagnosis.policy_at_workflow_head: The guard samples every 15 seconds, requires three consecutive healthy watches to clear a pending CPU episode, and expires the episode 75 seconds after its first bad watch (2 unsafe plus 3 healthy sample intervals). CPU busy is at least 0.75; high one-minute load is at least 0.75 per logical CPU together with busy at least 0.60.
resource_diagnosis.current_timeline: First bad watch 20:04:02Z (busy 0.93, load 10.29 on four logical CPUs); later watches alternated healthy and busy. The last busy watch was 20:05:06Z (busy 1.00). Native child exited 0 at 20:05:07Z. At 20:05:23Z the next sample was healthy (busy 0.02), but the 75-second episode deadline had passed before that sample was evaluated, and there had not been three consecutive healthy watches. Final invalidity follows the guard's specified rule.
resource_diagnosis.prior_member_comparison: The earlier member run 38168526559 did not expire a confirmation window: its first bad watch was 19:40:31Z (busy 1.00), one healthy pending watch followed at 19:40:47Z, and its native child exited 1 at 19:40:57Z while CPU confirmation remained pending. That run finalized invalid immediately with RESOURCE_CPU_BUSY.
resource_diagnosis.contention_boundary: SEO lane B attempt 2 completed at 20:00:09Z, before this acceptance step started at 20:02:21Z and before its first bad watch. Its overlap cannot explain this episode. Process attribution at the first bad watch included owned Chromium helpers alongside unrelated macOS lsd and SafariLaunchAgent activity; this single process snapshot does not identify one sole cause. The earlier run's snapshot was dominated by Chromium processes.
resource_diagnosis.conclusion: Measured host and Chromium CPU contention, with a finite confirmation deadline, explains the invalid final. The journals do not establish a guard implementation defect or a product failure.

product_verdict.reason: The acceptance resource final is invalid despite passing native assertions. No independent native acceptance review or valid hosted resource final exists for these member cases.

Immediately after terminal failure, MATRX_REVIEWER_MAGIC_LINK_JSON was deleted and a secret-name lookup verified its absence; the local link file was also verified absent. No link, token, email or profile identifier is stored here.
